sources.title: Hacker News Thread — Term Sheet, Please
claims: The release of *Term Sheet, Please* sparked immediate controversy on Hacker News, accumulating over 210 points and 80 comments within its first day of launch, according to discussions on Hacker News.

The game garnered 213 points and 85 comments on Hacker News within 12 hours, with several prominent commenters urging the creator to add a clear credit line linking back to the original game's homepage.
Beyond the copyright debate, players offered significant technical and user interface feedback on the Hacker News discussion.
sources.quote: Show HN: I recreated Papers Please but you're deciding which YC startups to fund (termsheetplease.com) 212 points by bolau 12 hours ago | hide | past | favorite | 84 comments
sources.reason: The Hacker News thread confirms the game 'Term Sheet, Please' (termsheetplease.com) received 212 points and 84 comments within 12 hours, with users debating copyright/attribution and providing technical/UI feedback.

sources.title: Asia Tech Review — YC Reaps Big Rewards
claims: In late 2025, YC secured nearly $200 million in cash through partial stake sales during the blockbuster public listings of its portfolio companies, as reported by Asia Tech Review.

Specifically, the public debut of the investment platform Groww in November 2025 netted YC approximately $117 million while leaving it with a 10% remaining stake worth roughly $1 billion, while the social commerce platform Meesho's transaction in December 2025 netted the accelerator about $10 million with $50 million in remaining stock, according to Asia Tech Review.

sources.title: Reddit — Why Has the Number of Indian Startups in YC Declined?
claims: This dramatic shift, discussed widely on Reddit, reflects a broader pivot toward global software-as-a-service and artificial intelligence.
sources.quote: Why has the number of Indian startups in Y Combinator batches dropped so sharply—from 64 in 2021 to just 1 in 2025?
sources.reason: The Reddit thread discusses the sharp drop in Indian startups in YC batches and attributes it to a shift in focus toward AI.
